identificationModule.briefTitle: Rupatadine in Patients With Ulcerative Colitis

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory condition that primarily targets the large intestine. Although substantial progress has been made in treatment modalities-especially with the development of immunomodulatory drugs and biologic therapies-managing UC continues to present significant challenges. At present, there is no definitive cure, and current treatment strategies are largely focused on controlling inflammation, relieving symptoms, and halting disease progression

armGroups.label: Control group
armGroups.description: control group (Mesalamine group) who will receive 1 g mesalamine three times daily for 3 months.

armGroups.label: Rupatadine
armGroups.description: (Rupatadine group) will receive 1 g mesalamine three times daily plus 20 mg rupatadine once daily for 3 months.

interventions.name: Mesalamine
interventions.description: Mesalamine or 5-amino salicylic acid (5-ASA), plays a crucial role in the treatment of ulcerative colitis (UC). It is the first-line therapy for mild to moderate cases of UC and is considered a cornerstone in its management.

interventions.name: Rupatadine
interventions.description: Rupatadine, a dual histamine H1 receptor and platelet-activating factor (PAF) receptor antagonist, has shown promising anti-inflammatory effects beyond its conventional use in allergic conditions

primaryOutcomes.description: The Partial Mayo Score (PMS) index will be utilized to ascertain the degree of disease severity. One non-invasive clinical measure for determining the severity of UC is the PMS. The composite score is derived from three subcategories: stool frequency, rectal bleeding, and physician's general assessment. The total score falls between 0 and 9

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years
* Both male and female will be included
* Mild and moderate UC patients are already diagnosed and confirmed by endoscope and histopathology.

Exclusion criteria:

* Breast feeding or pregnancy.
* Colorectal cancer patients.
* Patients with severe UC.
* Patients taking rectal or systemic steroids.
* Patients taking immunosuppressives or biological therapies.
* Addiction to alcohol and / or drugs.
* Known allergy to the studied medications.
